\[
\begin{gathered}
I_{\text{out}}(x,y) = I(x,y) - c\, \big(L \star I\big)(x,y)
= \sum_{j=-1}^{1} \sum_{i=-1}^{1} \big(\delta(i,j) - c\, L(i,j)\big)\, I(x+i,\, y+j),
\\[4pt]
c = 1, \quad \text{neighbors} = \text{4}
\end{gathered}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): Input channel value
- \(I_{\text{out}}\): Output channel value
- \(L\): The 3x3 Laplacian kernel with a negative center, 4 or 8 neighbors
- \(\delta\): Unit impulse, 1 at the center and 0 elsewhere
- \(c\): Amount
- \(\star\): Correlation

L is the discrete Laplacian with a negative center. It is positive where a pixel is darker than its neighbors and negative where it is brighter. Subtracting c times L makes bright pixels brighter and dark pixels darker next to an edge, so the edge gets steeper. The whole filter is one kernel whose weights add up to 1.
